How to Open a Business Bank Account in Pakistan for a New SECP Company

An exhaustive corporate banking tutorial for business owners and founders on opening a commercial bank account for a SECP Private Limited or Single Member Company (SMC-Pvt Ltd) in Pakistan, preparing Board Resolutions, and clearing NADRA biometric verification.

11 Min Read · Updated July 2026
State Bank of Pakistan Corporate Banking Guidelines
Corporate Banking Essential Checklist

1. The Role of Corporate Banking for SECP Entities

Once your company receives its digital Certificate of Incorporation from the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP), opening a corporate bank account is the next legal milestone.

Under Section 85 of the Companies Act 2017, company subscribers are legally mandated to deposit their subscribed paid-up capital into the corporate bank account within 30 days of incorporation.

3. Full List of SECP Certified Documents Required

Pakistani banks enforce strict Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Know Your Customer (KYC) regulations supervised by the State Bank of Pakistan:

Mandatory Document Dossier:

  • SECP Certified True Copies (CTC): Official certified copies of Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum of Association (MOA), and Articles of Association (AOA).
  • SECP Statutory Forms: Form 1 (Name Reservation), Form 21 (Registered Office Address Notification), and Form 29 (Particulars of Directors & Officers).
  • FBR Corporate NTN: Official 7-digit Corporate NTN certificate issued by the Federal Board of Revenue.
  • Identity Credentials: CNIC / NICOP copies of all proposed account signatories and directors.

4. Drafting an Approved Board Resolution

The company's Board of Directors must pass a formal resolution approving account opening:

Key Elements of a SBP-Compliant Board Resolution:

1. Bank & Branch Name: Explicitly naming the chosen commercial bank (e.g. Meezan Bank, Main Branch).

2. Account Signatories: Naming authorized directors who will operate the account.

3. Operating Instructions: Stating whether account is operated Singly (any one director) or Jointly (two directors combined).

4. Corporate Rubber Stamp: Signed and stamped by the Chief Executive or Company Secretary.
